errors.english: The engagement of the mind apprehending an entity produces an incompatible cause in the form of a latent impression, which the mind apprehending a non-entity then interrupts.
errors.why: It is the cognition of non-entity that, by producing an incompatible cause in the form of a latent impression, cuts off the continuum of the operating cognition of an entity; the English makes the entity-cognition produce its own incompatible cause.

note: A difficult apoha/virodha passage rendered closely and mostly correctly; one agent confusion in the account of how the non-entity cognition interrupts the entity cognition.

errors.english: an offense of concealing an infraction
errors.why: lhag ma is the specific offence class saṅghāvaśeṣa (concealing a saṅghāvaśeṣa offence), not a generic infraction.

note: Faithful rendering of the niśraya duties and the five-set qualifications; only the offence class is flattened.
Accurate translation of the Nyāyabindu commentary on the incomplete and unestablished pseudo-reasons, with root text and gloss kept distinct.

errors.why: da ltar byung ba'i sems is simply the presently arisen (present) mind; 'master-mind' is a garbled rendering.

errors.english: to refute what is harmful to the self
errors.why: bdag here is 'us/our position': the commentator introduces an opponent's objection that harms our thesis (no sentient beings, so no object of compassion) in order to refute it, not something harmful to 'the self'.

note: The analysis of past, future and present mind and the plantain simile are sound; one garbled term and a misread transition to the opponent's objection.

errors.english: Due to the power of intense attachment
errors.why: In Pramāṇa lhag par zhen pa is adhyavasāya, conceptual determination, not emotional attachment.

fix.find: Due to the power of intense attachment
fix.replace: Due to the power of conceptual determination (adhyavasāya)

errors.english: [note: original: "phyi rol pa rnams", likely referring to those who posit real universals outside the mind]
errors.why: The commentary itself immediately glosses phyi rol pa rnams as the particulars (what is external to the universal), not proponents of real universals.

fix.find: [note: original: "phyi rol pa rnams", likely referring to those who posit real universals outside the mind]
fix.replace: [note: original: "phyi rol pa rnams"; glossed below as the particulars, which are external to the universal]

errors.english: a mind thinking "this is the reality,"
errors.why: de kho na here is the cognition 'it is just that' (tad eva, a recognising judgement), not 'reality' (tattva).

errors.english: The appearance is [note: mistakenly taken as] the actual particular.
errors.why: This is Dharmottara's dṛśya/vikalpya pair: the 'appearing' (perceived) object is the particular and the conceptualised object is the universal, which ordinary users unify; the inserted 'mistakenly taken as' misreads the gloss.

note: The general apoha argument is followed, but key Pramāṇa terms (adhyavasāya, dṛśya) are mistranslated and a note contradicts the commentary it annotates.

errors.english: When that son of good family, the bodhisattva, the great being Dharmodgata, sits upon the Dharma throne and teaches the Dharma, we will prepare the Dharma throne for him
errors.why: The relative clause describes the throne: 'when we set up the Dharma throne on which that son of good family will sit and teach', not preparing it after he sits.

note: Faithful rendering of the abbreviated Sadāprarudita narrative with names and 'up to' markers handled correctly.

errors.english: If the head of (Indra) the king of gods
errors.why: This is Dharmakīrti's śakramūrdhan, 'Indra's head' as the name for an anthill (valmīka), the standard example; it is not Indra's literal head.

fix.find: If the head of (Indra) the king of gods

errors.english: such as a blue lotus (utpala) arising from slightly heavy [note: earthly] elements and so forth
errors.why: lci ba is cow dung (gomaya), the classic example of a plant arising from a heterogeneous cause; 'heavy elements' misreads it.

fix.find: such as a blue lotus (utpala) arising from slightly heavy [note: earthly] elements and so forth
fix.replace: such as a blue lotus (utpala) and the like arising from cow dung and so forth

errors.english: If it is certain in that way, how could it arise from something else?
errors.why: The full sentence on the side's first line ('Therefore, because place and time are fixed, that smoke is seen where [the cause is complete] and not seen when it is incomplete is its nature of being produced by that; otherwise it would not occur only sometimes') is not translated.

fix.find: If it is certain in that way, how could it arise from something else?
fix.replace: Therefore, because place and time are fixed, that smoke is seen where [its cause] is present and not seen where it is incomplete is its nature of being produced by that; otherwise it would not occur only sometimes. If it is certain in that way, how could it arise from something else?

note: The causal argument and the summary verses are followed, but the two classic examples (anthill, cow dung) are mistranslated and the opening sentence is dropped.

errors.english: Moon must be separated from his captivating mind one line of text regarding the King's reaction
errors.why: The phrase 'one line of text regarding the King's reaction' is a stray editorial remark with nothing corresponding in the Tibetan.

fix.find: captivating mind one line of text regarding the King's reaction

errors.english: He possessed noble qualities and fine intelligence, becoming a worthy object of great praise.
errors.why: This opens a four-line verse on merit versus birth, which the English turns into narrative prose about Moon.

errors.english: Even in some great beings, superficiality is prevented by the limit of their birth.
errors.why: The verse's point, supported by the following 'for men of great lineage are seen to be like dogs', is that high birth does not guard against the fault of baseness, so saying it is 'prevented' contradicts the argument.

note: The narrative is followed, but the gnomic verse is partly turned into prose and its point is muddled, and a stray editorial phrase was left in the text.

errors.english: what is called substance consists of two types of meaning: the external object and the consciousness
errors.why: Substance is defined as the conditioned entity (pot etc.) that can accomplish, without depending on anything else, the two kinds of purpose related to object and cognition; it does not 'consist of' object and consciousness.

note: Sound rendering of the observation/non-observation and substance/quality discussion, apart from one misparsed definition of substance.
A careful rendering of the Vinaya commentary on the building rule, with root-text lemmata, the Upāliparipṛcchā citation and the question-and-answer structure all correct.
